f.title: Manage trial records for integrity, traceability and privacy
f.statement: Clinical trials shall incorporate efficient and robust processes for managing records (including data) so that record integrity and traceability are maintained and personal information is protected, allowing accurate reporting, interpretation and verification.
f.applicability: Clinical medical research (clinical trials) approved by EDA in Egypt (scope: safety reporting, safety monitoring and related record keeping only)

f.title: Retain essential records securely and make them available on request
f.statement: Essential records shall be retained securely by sponsors and investigators for the required period and be available to regulatory authorities, monitors, auditors and IRBs/IECs on request.

f.title: Submit progress reports every 4 months until site close-out
f.statement: The applicant shall submit progress follow-up reports (Follow-up template) to Bio-Inn-EDA and the Supreme Council simultaneously via the EDA Clinical Trial Platform and e-mail every 4 months from the EDA approval date until close-out of all sites in Egypt, within a maximum of 15 days after the data lock point; serious breaches, protocol deviations and local non-serious AE line listings are included.
f.applicability: Clinical medical research (clinical trials) approved by EDA in Egypt (scope: safety reporting, safety monitoring and related record keeping only)

f.title: Grade adverse event intensity as mild, moderate or severe
f.statement: Intensity of an AE or ADR is graded: Grade 1 mild (transient, no special treatment, no interference with daily activities); Grade 2 moderate (some inconvenience, ameliorated by simple measures); Grade 3 severe (intolerable, significantly interrupting normal life, requiring systemic therapy).
f.applicability: Clinical medical research (clinical trials) approved by EDA in Egypt (scope: safety reporting, safety monitoring and related record keeping only)

f.title: Apply the seriousness criteria, including important medical events
f.statement: A serious adverse event or reaction is any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose results in death, is life-threatening, requires or prolongs inpatient hospitalisation, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, is a congenital anomaly/birth defect, or is an important medical event that may jeopardise the patient or require intervention; the latter shall usually be considered serious.
f.applicability: Clinical medical research (clinical trials) approved by EDA in Egypt (scope: safety reporting, safety monitoring and related record keeping only)

rows.quote: These shall also usually be considered serious.
rows.review_note: Review: checked against source, no change. Double-check: quote, level and actor confirmed.

f.title: Assess causality using the stated categories; use the WHO AEFI method for vaccines
f.statement: Unless the protocol specifies otherwise, causality is assessed as certain, probable/likely, possible, unlikely, unassessable or not related; for vaccines the WHO "Causality assessment of an adverse event following immunization (AEFI)" shall be followed.
f.applicability: Clinical medical research (clinical trials) approved by EDA in Egypt (scope: safety reporting, safety monitoring and related record keeping only)

rows.quote: In case of vaccines “Causality assessment of an adverse event following immunization (AEFI)” Shall be followed.

f.title: Document and submit any delegation of safety reporting to the sponsor or CRO
f.statement: The PI may delegate safety reporting to the sponsor or a CRO; any delegation and the PI-sponsor/CRO safety communication process shall be formally documented and submitted to EDA via the Clinical Trial Platform and e-mail. When delegated, the sponsor/CRO assumes responsibility for all immediate SAE notifications and initial and follow-up reports, submitted simultaneously to Bio-Inn and the Supreme Council.

f.statement: Other safety issues qualify for expedited reporting where they might materially alter the benefit-risk assessment or warrant changes in IMP administration or trial conduct, e.g. SAEs associated with trial procedures, major new animal safety findings, DMC recommendations relevant to participant safety, and post-study SUSARs reported to the investigator.
